content: Stool softeners are prescribed to alleviate constipation on a short-term basis, particularly for individuals who need to avoid straining during bowel movements due to conditions such as heart problems, hemorrhoids, or other medical issues. These medications work by softening the stool, making it easier to pass. In some cases, stool softeners may be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Stool softeners are available in various forms, including capsules, tablets, liquids, and syrups, and are taken orally. They are typically taken at bedtime. Follow the instructions provided on the packaging or prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as directed, without exceeding or reducing the prescribed dose or frequency. Capsules and tablets should be taken with a full glass of water. If using the liquid form, it comes with a specially marked dropper for accurate dosing; ask your pharmacist for guidance if needed. To mask the bitter taste of the liquid (not the syrup), mix it with 4 ounces of milk, fruit juice, or formula. It usually takes one to three days of regular use for the medication to take effect. Do not use stool softeners for more than one week unless directed by your doctor. If you experience sudden changes in bowel habits lasting longer than two weeks or if your stools remain hard after one week of use, contact your doctor. Before taking stool softeners, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to any medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially aspirin and vitamins. Do not take mineral oil while using stool softeners. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking stool softeners, inform your doctor immediately. If you forget to take a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Stool softeners may cause mild side effects, such as stomach or intestinal cramps, upset stomach, or throat irritation (from oral liquids). If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, such as skin rash (hives), difficulty breathing or swallowing, fever, vomiting, or stomach pain, require immediate medical attention. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on safe disposal. If you have any questions about taking this medication, ask your pharmacist for clarification.
